required_facts.fact: In 2177, an Alliance Marine unit is sent to investigate the settlement at Akuze, a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space, after all contact is lost with the pioneer team. The unit arrives to find the settlement intact but completely abandoned—no survivors are found. When the unit establishes camp for the night, they are attacked by subterranean thresher maws, creatures the Alliance has never encountered before. The unit is nearly completely slaughtered in the attack, with fifty marines killed and only one known survivor reaching the landing zone alive. If Commander Shepard is that sole survivor, Shepard is permanently marked by the trauma. Years later, Corporal Toombs is discovered to have also survived the attack. Toombs reveals a shocking truth: the massacre was not an accident. According to Toombs' testimony, the renegade black ops group Cerberus deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines as part of an experiment to study the creatures and observe how the unit responded to an unknown threat. Toombs was captured by Cerberus after the attack and subjected to horrific ordeals including being injected with thresher maw acid as part of their research. The revelation that Cerberus orchestrated the massacre haunts Shepard throughout the trilogy, becoming a symbol of Cerberus's willingness to sacrifice human lives for their research agenda.

Tali'Zorah vas Neema, a young quarian woman who was one of Commander Shepard's most loyal companions during the fight against Saren, has earned her adult name through service and has been integrated into the Migrant Fleet as a full citizen. The Admiralty Board of the quarian fleet assigns her to a classified research mission to investigate anomalous activity in the star of Haestrom, a quarian colony world long abandoned to the geth after their extinction event. The primary objective is to study the planet's rapidly dying sun to understand its unusual behavior. Tali's strike team, including experienced marine commander Kal'Reegar, is deployed to Haestrom to conduct on-site observations. However, the team encounters unexpectedly fierce geth resistance, including multiple troop types (Troopers, Rocket Troopers, Hunters, Destroyers, Recon Drones, Primes, and even a towering Geth Colossus) and extreme solar radiation that strips kinetic and biotic shields, forcing Shepard's squad to navigate between safe shaded areas. When Shepard arrives to investigate Tali's team, they find all of the quarian marines slain except for Kal'Reegar, the sole survivor. Shepard must navigate the research facility while contending with Geth forces and the lethal radiation. The mission culminates at an observatory where Tali has positioned herself with final defensive measures. To advance, Shepard must retrieve two demolition charges from nearby structures to destroy a pillar blocking the path forward. In the final confrontation, the Geth Colossus—equipped with a powerful self-repair ability—presents a formidable obstacle. Shepard has the choice to use a Paragon interrupt to convince Kal'Reegar to stand down from providing covering fire, or to permit him to continue firing at the risk of his own death. Shepard must close to melee range to permanently disable the Colossus' regeneration protocol, destroy the construct, and eliminate waves of geth reinforcements. After the battle, Tali is successfully recruited and evacuated to the Normandy SR-2. If Kal'Reegar survives, he uploads the mission data to the Admiralty Board; if he does not survive, Tali uploads it herself, tormented by the loss of her entire team. Tali integrates into the Normandy's main engineering section alongside Gabriella Daniels and Kenneth Donnelly. Her father, Admiral Rael'Zorah, sends a message confirming her approved transfer and warning that negligence leading to her death will bring severe consequences. The mission's non-completion would prevent Tali from being recruited and would guarantee squad deaths during the suicide mission due to inability to upgrade the Normandy's shields.

evidence.text: Shepard Confronts Toombs Holding Dr. Wayne Hostage. 2183, during the UNC: Dead Scientists assignment Ontarom, in the back room of a cramped mercenary-held facility Corporal Toombs was one of the Alliance marines who survived the thresher maw massacre at Akuze in 2177. Cerberus had deliberately set the maws on his unit as an experiment and, when Toombs was found alive, Cerberus captured him for years of horrific study, including injections of thresher maw acid. After escaping confinement, Toombs began systematically hunting down the scientists responsible, enlisting mercenary help. Commander Shepard investigating a series of dead Alliance scientists crossed paths with Toombs on Ontarom as he was about to kill Dr. Wayne, the last scientist on his list.

Thresher maws were enormous subterranean carnivores that spent their lives eating or hunting for food, bursting from the ground without warning when disturbed. They reproduced via spores that could lie dormant for millennia and survive deep space and atmospheric re-entry, so maw spores appeared on many worlds, spread by earlier generations of space travelers, possibly predating the asari.

They lived alone in large underground nests, growing over 30 meters above ground with a body nearly twice that size beneath the surface; an adult's body never fully left the ground, with only the head and tentacles erupting to attack. They fed through an unusual photosynthesis using absorbed solar radiation plus minerals and ores consumed from the ground, favoring bodies with little or no atmosphere. Mostly immobile above ground, they moved at high speed while burrowing, absorbed tremendous damage, and attacked by spitting viscous acid, bursting up beneath prey, and smashing targets with their claws while emitting infrasound. Shields were completely ineffective against them.

The Alliance first encountered thresher maws on the colony of Akuze in 2177, where they killed nearly an entire marine rescue force. If Shepard has the Sole Survivor background, Shepard alone survived; Corporal Toombs, met later on Ontarom, claimed Cerberus deliberately caused the Akuze massacre to study the maws and held him captive for experiments, and Cerberus later used the same tactic to lure Admiral Kahoku's team into a nest on Edolus. Maws are found on many uncharted worlds, usually one per planet, including Antibaar, Chohe, Nepheron, Nonuel, Presrop, Xawin, Trebin and Edolus.

In Mass Effect 2, a thresher maw is the final test of Clan Urdnot's Rite of Passage on Tuchanka, lured to the proving grounds by ground-pounding pistons to attack Grunt's krantt. Gatatog Uvenk notes that the last krogan to kill a maw on foot was Urdnot Wrex. In Mass Effect 3, Kalros, a legendary maw called "the mother from which all other thresher maws spawn" and the largest ever seen, roams Tuchanka near the Shroud facility. Shepard activates two maw hammers to summon her against a Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud; she coils around it and drags it underground. Her size prompts Javik to remark that maws are now too big to ride, implying they were smaller in Prothean times. The concept was confirmed by art director Derek Watts to draw on Dune's sandworms, and also resembles D&D Ankhegs, the Star Wars Sarlacc, and the real Bobbit worm.

A thresher maw shows up during Grunt's Rite of Passage into Clan Urdnot after all other predators have been neutralized. Lured to the proving grounds by persistent ground pounding by a giant piston in the complex, the maw proceeds to attack Grunt's krantt as the final test of the krogan's skill. If the thresher is slain within a set time limit, Gatatog Uvenk informs Shepard that no krogan has slain a thresher maw on foot in generations; the last one to accomplish this feat was Urdnot Wrex. EDI also tells Shepard that defeating the thresher maw has generated several breeding requests for Grunt and even one for Shepard. Jubilant krogan in the Urdnot Camp can be heard exclaiming that they will be eating "thresher steaks" for months. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Thresher Maw! This is not so much a wave as it is a giant creature attack. There is only one Thresher Maw and the primary objective is simply to survive. All you have to do is survive the attack for five minutes and the test will be ended, though there are additional dialogue accolades if you succeed in taking it down. If you manage to kill the Thresher Maw, you gain the respect of the krogan and the Rite ends. The Thresher Maw moves around the outskirts of the map, but its trail of flying dirt clods is easy to follow when it dives back underground. The Thresher Maw can destroy the "merely metal" structures, so try to avoid those for cover and go for the sturdier stone/concrete pillars and walls instead. Its acid spit is an area of effect attack and will accurately shoot at you even if you're cloaked. The blue tongue is **not** a weak spot—shooting it does not cause any additional damage. **Combat Strategy:** There is one indestructible stone pillar on the low ground area of the level—to the right as you face out from the keystone—that you can use to take cover from the Maw from any direction it might appear. Additionally, there are two respawning thermal clips at the base of this pillar as well as easy access to a medi\-gel and power cells on the higher ground that you can pick up from the edge of the raised area without needing to climb up. This is without a doubt the optimal place to fight the Maw, as all other locations will involve considerable running about when the Maw moves. Place your squadmates in cover behind the other two indestructible pillars on the high ground and they should also be safe and might even draw the Maw's fire giving you free rein. If a squadmate does go down it's not the end of the world: Shepard alone is more than enough to beat the Maw even on Insanity. **Combat Tips:** - The metal pillars can be destroyed by the Thresher Maw in one hit, but any cover made of stone/concrete is not destructible. You should always try to interpose indestructible cover between yourself and the Maw. The Maw's spit projectile does have an area of effect so try to be as completely in cover as possible when the Maw attacks to ensure you are not hit. - Shepard's shields take longer than usual to recover after an acid hit, so be careful. On the plus side it takes about three consecutive hits to kill Shepard even on Insanity. Don't hesitate to use a medi\-gel to quickly restore your shields (provided you have the Emergency Shielding medi\-gel upgrade). - A well\-upgraded heavy pistol is more than sufficient to take out the Maw as long as you take advantage of respawning thermal clips to keep replenishing its ammo. - On Insanity, the Thresher Maw's sheer amount of health makes using heavy weapons inefficient. Conventional weapons modded with anti\-armor ammo powers are your best bet. - Though nominally ineffective against armor, Grunt's Concussive Shot can still "stagger" the Maw, reducing the number of acid shots it will take before retreating. - Zaeed's Inferno Grenade, Mordin's Incinerate, and Samara's Reave are examples of good squadmate attacks to use. Using weapons with high armor penetration such as the Widow, M\-76 Revenant, M\-96 Mattock, or most pistols will help a lot. - The Cain will usually only damage half the Thresher Maw's health on Insanity. - The Thresher Maw is immune to the effects of Stasis.

**Kalros**, a legendary thresher maw known as "the mother from which all other thresher maws spawn" and the largest thresher maw yet seen, plays a major part in the ongoing Reaper war of 2186\. She roams Tuchanka's wastelands near the salarians' Shroud facility, acting as a natural deterrent to the vital installation. A mural found within the ancient krogan city nearby that Shepard explores prominently depicts Kalros, indicating that she is at least as old as the city itself. She is summoned to attack a Reaper Destroyer that is guarding the Shroud. Shepard activates two maw hammers that pound the ground to call her, and she responds in the way her territorial instincts tell her. She attacks and defeats the Destroyer by coiling around it and pulling it into the ground, clearing the path to the Shroud. Kalros' size may cause Javik to remark that thresher maws are now too big to ride, indicating that the maws were much smaller during the Protheans' time.

- The concept of the thresher maw appears to have been drawn from multiple sources both fiction and nonfiction. - Thresher maws appear to be inspired by the giant sandworms of Frank Herbert's *Dune*. This is somewhat substantiated by the use of maw hammers in Mass Effect 3 to summon Kalros. Similar devices called "thumpers" were used to attract sandworms in the *Dune* novels. Additionally, Javik's remark about thresher maws being ridden draws parallel to *Dune*'s desert\-dwelling Fremen routinely riding sandworms when travelling long distances. This inspiration was confirmed by art director Derek Watts. - Thresher maws are strikingly similar to Ankhegs that appeared in the original *Dungeons \& Dragons* game and later, in BioWare's Baldur's Gate. Both creatures burrow underground, surprise attack from beneath, have worm\-like bodies with insect heads, and spit acid. - The thresher maw may also be inspired by the Sarlacc, a creature present in the *Star Wars* universe, as the two bear many similarities, particularly in terms of interplanetary migration. - In real life the creatures share aspects of both physical resemblance and predatory traits with an ocean\-dwelling species of polychaete known as the Bobbit Worm.

Corporal Toombs was one of the Alliance marines at Akuze and a survivor of the thresher maw tragedy there. Cerberus had set the thresher maws on his unit as an experiment; when Toombs was found alive afterward, Cerberus was delighted and hauled him off for further study, subjecting him to horrific ordeals over years, including injection with thresher maw acid.

Toombs eventually escaped confinement and, deeply traumatized, began systematically hunting the scientists responsible, hiring mercenary help. If Commander Shepard investigated a series of dead Alliance scientists, they crossed paths with Toombs on Ontarom as he was about to kill the last one, Dr. Wayne. Shepard could talk him down by promising a public trial for Wayne and psychological treatment for Toombs; allow Toombs his revenge; kill Wayne personally under Spectre authority; or shoot Toombs to save the scientist, then send the Fifth Fleet to take Wayne for trial. If Shepard had the Sole Survivor background and spared Wayne while stopping Toombs, Toombs noted that the vids said Shepard was the only one to escape Akuze, said "who am I to argue?" and killed himself.

If Toombs survived the 2183 encounter, he sent Shepard a message in 2185 titled "What the hell?" after learning of Shepard's ties to Cerberus, feeling betrayed and promising retribution: "I've got my own merc team now, Shepard. And I kill any Cerberus team I can find. If I run into you, don't expect any different." Galactic News reports could describe his activities: if both he and Wayne survived, an independent inquiry against Cerberus proceeded on their testimony; if Wayne died, the inquiry dismissed Toombs' claims as those of a disturbed man lacking evidence.

Thresher maws now spit a spread of acid balls rather than a single one, and they can lead their target. When a thresher maw goes underground, it stays underground longer. A trail of rocks and upended earth now indicates the direction the creature is moving in. The thresher maw has a chance to deploy multiple Sensory Tentacles around its lair when it retreats underground. These tentacles are immobile but can deal damage on targets within striking range. The thresher maw then actively seeks out its potential victims' location and will deal the killing blow from below when near enough.

Akuze was a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space. In 2177, while Akuze was still in the early stages of colonization, all contact was lost with the pioneer team. An Alliance Marine unit sent to investigate found the settlement intact but no survivors. When the unit camped for the night, it was attacked by thresher maws. Fifty marines were lost and only one reached the landing zone alive.

In Mass Effect, if Commander Shepard was the sole known survivor, C-Sec officer Eddie Lang on the Citadel mentioned a monument at Akuze with a section dedicated to Shepard. Shepard could later learn of a second survivor, Corporal Toombs, who claimed the slaughter was not an accident: he said the black ops group Cerberus had deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines to study the creatures and observe how the unit reacted.

In Mass Effect 2, a survivor Shepard could see news of a Shepard Memorial being erected on Akuze, with a commemoration ceremony hosted by Admiral Steven Hackett planned for 2186 once the site was cleared of thresher maws. If Shepard had rescued Toombs in 2183, he sent a threatening message about Shepard's new alliance with Cerberus. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, after Shepard and Liara defeated Tela Vasir, the asari Spectre cited the Akuze massacre as evidence of Shepard's hypocrisy in allying with Cerberus, the group responsible for those deaths. In Mass Effect 3, a survivor Shepard could view a recording on Cronos Station of a Cerberus scientist and the Illusive Man confirming that Cerberus was behind the attack.

If Commander Shepard has the Sole Survivor background, Shepard alone survived the thresher attack on Akuze. However, a second survivor may be encountered later at a facility on Ontarom. Corporal Toombs, leader of a group of mercenaries who stormed this facility, claims that a black\-ops group called Cerberus caused the massacre at Akuze deliberately. He says Cerberus scientists wanted to study the thresher maws, so they let them kill not only the colonists, but the marine rescue team as well, to watch and study. Cerberus was delighted that Toombs survived and held him captive for years, using him for experiments. It is likely Toombs' story is true, as Cerberus used a similar technique six years later, luring Admiral Kahoku's marine team to their deaths in a thresher nest on Edolus. Thresher maws are encountered on a number of uncharted worlds. There is usually only one per planet, but some have two. They are usually encountered in the Mako, but can be fought on foot as well, though this is exceedingly dangerous. The maws that are encountered can be bypassed if necessary. Planets known to have thresher maws are Antibaar, Chohe, Nepheron, Nonuel, Presrop, Xawin, Trebin, and Edolus. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

After years of being experimented on, somehow Toombs managed to escape his confinement. "UNC: Dead Scientists" was a Mass Effect assignment obtained either from a security terminal on Noveria's Port Hanshan Mezzanine (initially labeled "Doctor at Risk") or from Admiral Hackett when Shepard traveled to the Newton system. Someone was killing every Alliance scientist who had worked on a classified project years earlier on Akuze, the planet where Shepard's entire unit was wiped out if Shepard had the Sole Survivor background. The last surviving project member, Dr. Wayne, was believed to be hiding in the Newton system of the Kepler Verge.

The assignment played out on the planet Ontarom, where Shepard fought through human mercenaries and snipers outside and krogan-backed mercenaries in a cramped, crate-filled facility. In a back room Shepard found Corporal Toombs holding Dr. Wayne hostage. Toombs revealed that after a thresher maw attack killed the rest of his squad, he had been captured by scientists working for Cerberus and used as a test subject; he had been killing the responsible scientists in revenge. Wayne repeatedly called Toombs crazy and demanded Shepard shoot him. With enough Charm (10+ points), Shepard could talk Toombs down and have the Alliance arrest Wayne; with enough Intimidate (8+), Shepard could shoot Wayne. Failing to defuse the standoff resulted in Toombs killing Wayne and then himself. If Toombs and Wayne both survived, both testified against Cerberus in Mass Effect 2 (Wayne given immunity for cooperation), and Toombs could later message Shepard expressing disgust at Shepard joining Cerberus and threatening to kill Cerberus operatives, including the Commander. If Wayne was shot via Intimidate, Toombs' testimony was dismissed for insufficient evidence.

Toombs had been killing the scientists responsible in revenge. When he tells his story to Shepard, he will describe his escape from Cerberus in two ways: 1. If you finished the UNC: Hades' Dogs assignment, Toombs comments that he managed to escape because someone already took Cerberus down. 2. Otherwise, Toombs' escape will not be explained \- only that he managed to escape. Morality points can be obtained based on your decisions. If you have at least 10 points in Charm, you can convince Corporal Toombs to lower his weapon and let the Alliance authorities arrest the scientist. If you have 8 or more points in Intimidate, you can shoot the scientist yourself (you can still let Toombs do the shooting, but he kills himself afterward). If you shoot Toombs, the scientist will give you credits as a reward, but you can still arrest him afterwards. If Shepard is a Sole Survivor, the initial confrontation has Toombs recognizing Shepard, and Shepard in turn blurts out he was presumed dead on Akuze along with everyone else in their unit. Because there are two witnesses to the attack—Shepard and Toombs—the scientist has a weaker argument on Toombs being just a regular crazy this time. Because of your background and shared experience with Toombs, the option to shoot him does not appear when he wants you to decide what happens next. Instead you can egg him on or beg him to reconsider, which will result in the same outcome as the above: dead scientist and suicided Toombs. He thinks making this public is a futile effort as Cerberus would not let their activities be exposed. The only way to avoid Toombs killing the scientist and then himself is to use the Charm or Intimidate options, and if the latter, you'll have to shoot the scientist yourself instead of letting Toombs do it. All outcomes result in a text display describing the aftermath, followed by an immediate exit of the bunker on closing the notice. You can still reenter in case you haven't finished looting. A monitor in the room with Toombs and the scientist can be interacted with, though it does nothing other than display a ship schematic. The assignment is marked complete upon returning to the Normandy and accessing the Galaxy Map. Admiral Hackett provides further details on the aftermath of your decision.

- Even on Shepards without the Sole Survivor background, choosing the Paragon option results in Toombs complaining you "got away with a few scratches and a scary reputation" as if Shepard was also involved in the thresher maw incident. - This assignment is referred to as "(UNC:) Survivor's Revenge" in the game's internal data. |  | **The following information is drawn from cut content and is not to be considered canon in any way.** | | --- | --- |

In 2183, Commander Shepard may encounter Cerberus, investigate their activities and discover they conducted experiments intended to create supersoldiers, including experiments on rachni and Thorian Creepers. The organization accidentally unleashed rachni on Listening Posts Alpha and Theta when their experimental subjects, which were shipped from Noveria, escaped from Depot Sigma\-23. They are also involved with a settlement on Chasca whose colonial pioneer team was converted into Husks. In addition, a traumatised marine named Corporal Toombs claims that Cerberus lured thresher maws to the colony on Akuze, resulting in the notorious massacre there; Toombs was one of the only survivors. Soon after the massacre Toombs was captured and withstood brutal experiments. Things may come to a head if Shepard fully explores the disappearance of a group of marines under Rear Admiral Kahoku and finds that Cerberus had lured them to a thresher maw nest using a distress beacon much like on Akuze. After being informed of the marines' fate, Kahoku purchases information from the Shadow Broker and asks Shepard to track Cerberus down. During his investigation, Kahoku comes to the conclusion that Cerberus is in fact a rogue black\-ops group that had broken away from the Alliance. Soon after relaying this information to Shepard, however, Kahoku is captured and killed. His body is discovered in a Cerberus facility on Binthu, which also holds the location for Cerberus' alleged main base on Nepheron. #### Cerberus Forces Cerberus bases are usually guarded by the following forces: - **Cerberus Anti\-Tanks:** These units are on patrol outside the base and are armed with assault rifles that have the ability to fire rockets by switching fire mode\[1], which \- fitting with their name \- they tend to use against the Mako. - **Cerberus Commandos:** Highly trained shock troops armed with assault rifles or pistols. - **Cerberus Snipers:** Often found indoors, these snipers find cover and hit you with Assassination. - **Research Technicians:** The technicians are normally biotics; though unarmored, they use powerful Throw attacks. The bases also contain whatever dangerous experimental subjects Cerberus is currently working on, which includes rachni (soldiers and workers) and Thorian Creepers. |  | ***“I said get back!”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Redemption** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.page: Tali'Zorah vas Normandy — Character Analysis (Part 2) — Mass Effect 2: Leadership and Family
evidence.text: **Summary:** Part 2 of a character analysis of Tali'Zorah. Covers Mass Effect 2: her older, more confident look and the name change from "nar Rayya" to "vas Neema," her command of a squad of quarian marines, Haestrom and Kal'Reegar, the Normandy crew's regard for her, and her two parental figures — Auntie Shala'Raan (family) and her father Rael'Zorah (duty) — plus quarian immunodeficiency and suit-linking as the culture's deepest gesture of trust. Part 3 covers the treason trial and her fatal flaw.

There is one Colossus present on Haestrom, which acts as a level boss at the end of the mission to recruit Tali'Zorah vas Neema. A notable trait of this particular Colossus is that it is the Armature steel\-gray, not white. Interestingly, the quarian marine Kal'Reegar calls the Colossus an "Armature\-class" unit, indicating that at least quarians see it as a variation of the Armature. There are also multiple Colossi on the Firewalker Pack, but they are fought with the Hammerhead and lack the self\-repair mechanism, making them much less challenging.

Kal'Reegar is a marine of the quarian Migrant Fleet who Commander Shepard meets on the former quarian colony of Haestrom in the Far Rim. He is part of a squad of Migrant Fleet Marines assigned to protect Tali'Zorah vas Neema, who was on the planet doing research on the system's sun. After arrival on Haestrom, the quarians are attacked by geth, who proceed to slaughter most of the expedition, except for Reegar and Tali. When Shepard encounters him, he is held up on one side of a bridge, taking potshots with a ML\-77 Missile Launcher at a geth platoon attempting to gain access to the observatory Tali is working in. The platoon includes a Geth Colossus, which is giving Reegar trouble. His suit is punctured and he is injured. Nonetheless, Reegar is reluctant to do anything but fight and jokingly takes offense if Shepard points out the tear in his bio\-suit. The Commander can either convince him to stand down and cover their back or accept his help in taking down the Colossus. Whatever be the case, the geth platoon is taken down and Tali is rescued. After Shepard arrives at the observatory and talks to Tali (and if Reegar has survived the battle), Reegar will come in and say he's injured and has already called for a pick\-up. However, Tali informs him that she will not be returning to the flotilla but will join Shepard on the Normandy instead. Before they part ways, Tali gives Kal the data she obtained about the planet's sun so he can give it to the Admiralty Board. Should Commander Shepard not insist that Kal'Reegar sit out the battle with the Geth Colossus, and then take too much time during the battle, Kal'Reegar will die. Should he survive, Shepard can ask Tali on the Normandy about Kal's condition, revealing that he recovered from his injuries having sustained just a minor infection and is no worse for the wear.

evidence.text: When Shepard recruits her for the Suicide Mission, on Haestrom, her whole squad is willing to die for her — including Kal'Reegar ("We don't have enough people on our side for you to take one for the team. Stand down."). She questions whether the losses were worth the research the Admiralty Board demanded: "A lot of people died here. Some of them were my friends. All of them were good at their jobs. That damn data better be worth it." In the *Lair of the Shadow Broker* DLC, surveillance shows her trying and failing to write letters home to the families of the men who died protecting her, saving draft after draft.

Kal'Reegar was a quarian marine of the Migrant Fleet Marines. In Mass Effect 2, Commander Shepard met him on the former quarian colony of Haestrom in the Far Rim, where he was part of a squad assigned to protect Tali'Zorah vas Neema during her research on the system's dying sun. Geth attacked and killed most of the expedition, leaving only Reegar and Tali. Shepard found him pinned at a bridge, firing a missile launcher at a geth platoon including a Geth Colossus that was trying to reach Tali's observatory. His suit was punctured and he was injured, but he was reluctant to stand down; Shepard could order him to hold back or accept his help against the Colossus. If Shepard took too long in the fight without benching him, Reegar was killed; if he survived, he recovered with only a minor infection.

If he survived Haestrom, Shepard could meet him again during Tali's loyalty mission on the flotilla, where he was one of few quarians who publicly held Tali in high regard during her treason trial and could testify to her character. He argued that a war to reclaim the homeworld from the geth would be futile and harmful to the Fleet, though he would never shirk his military duty. If Shepard rallied the crowd, Reegar declared Tali had done more for the Fleet than any Admiral and said that if she were exiled, he should be too. Admirals Raan and Gerrel sought his opinion and accepted his recommendation to let Tali retake the Alarei. He was afterward assigned to escort quarian techs investigating the dark energy buildup.

In Mass Effect 3, if the quarians survived their war with the geth and Reegar had survived Haestrom, Shepard received an email that Reegar and his squad had died on Palaven repairing and protecting a communications tower relaying critical information to the Turian Hierarchy. The Reegar Carbine was named after his family of marines; cut content gave his full name as Kal'Reegar vas Lomas.

In 2185, Kal'Reegar and a dozen of his Marines accompanied Tali'Zorah vas Neema to the planet Haestrom, a former quarian colony now under geth control. Reegar's forces were tasked with the protection of the science team as they examined the strange nature of the system's sun, but most of the Marines were slaughtered by a company of geth troops, leaving Reegar as one of the two survivors of the task force. Later, a squad of quarian marines attempt to clear the small science ship known as the Alarei after it is overrun by geth. However, they are unsuccessful, with every marine involved in the raid being killed. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Kal'Reegar dies in the Reaper War if he survived Haestrom and the quarians survived their war to retake Rannoch. The message is received sometime after Thessia's fall. **ANN Alert: New Article on "Quarian Fleet"** --- From: Alliance News Network Information Partners Palaven \- The Turian Hierarchy, one of the most powerful and respected ground forces in the galaxy, are today paying respects to an unlikely ally: the marines of the Quarian Fleet. The weakened immune systems of quarians normally means their forces are restricted to ships. But when an emergency technical team was required to repair a ground\-based com relay, providing vital intel to the turian military, one quarian squad stepped up. Commanded by squad leader Kal'Reegar, the quarian team repaired the com system, then sacrificed their lives holding the position until krogan troops arrived. When turian troops offered to provide evac support, Reegar refused, insisting they could not risk the relay falling. He said multiple breaches to their exo\-suits made evacuation impossible. "We're all dead anyway," Reegar reportedly said. "Just make them pay for it." A spokesman for Primarch Victus praised the squad's bravery. "Whatever our past politics, today the galaxy stands together against a single threat," Victus said. "We are humbled by the sacrifice of our allies from Rannoch, and we promise to return the honor."

Tali's Trial Aboard the Rayya. 2185, some time after Tali rejoined Shepard the liveship Rayya at the Migrant Fleet — the garden plaza, then the hearing chamber If Kal'Reegar lived through Haestrom, he is in the crowd — one of the few quarians who openly respects Tali — and can be called as a character witness. Asked what the quarians should do about a homeworld, he says a war with the geth to retake it would be futile and bad for the Fleet, though he would never shirk his duty. Raan and Gerrel seek out his read on the trial and take his advice to let Tali retake the Alarei to win the crowd. If Shepard rallies the room, Reegar steps up beside Veetor'Nara, says Tali has done more for the Fleet than any admiral, and that if she is exiled he should be too. Afterward he tells Tali he only spoke because Shepard did, and notes she never mentioned her evidence.

Tali: Treason was Tali'Zorah's loyalty mission in Mass Effect 2, acquired some time after recruiting her when Kelly Chambers noted Tali seemed distraught. The Migrant Fleet's Admiralty Board had charged Tali with treason for smuggling active geth into the flotilla; on her father Admiral Rael'Zorah's orders she had been sending deactivated geth samples home. The Normandy, a registered Cerberus vessel, docked with the liveship Rayya via Tali's passphrase. Captain Kar'Danna met the squad; if Legion was brought, Shepard needed Charm or Intimidate to keep it aboard. Admiral Shala'Raan greeted Tali as "Tali'Zorah vas Normandy," revealing the Board had already stripped her quarian ship-name, a bad omen. Raan, recused from judging due to her closeness to the family, opened proceedings, and Shepard served as Tali's advocate.

The admirals sprang the news that the lab ship Alarei had been overrun by geth and that Rael'Zorah was presumed dead. Shepard and Tali proposed to retake the Alarei, and the hearing recessed. Speaking with the admirals, Veetor, and Kal'Reegar (present only if Veetor was returned to the Fleet and Kal'Reegar survived Haestrom) revealed the trial was a facade for the admirals' agendas: Xen wanted to study AI to reclaim the geth, Gerrel wanted war to retake Rannoch, Koris wanted Tali and her father made examples of, and Raan admitted she had deliberately withheld news of Rael's death so Tali's shock would win sympathy.

Aboard the Alarei, Shepard's team fought through waves of Geth Troopers, Hunters, a Geth Prime, and Combat Drones in close quarters, with Tali's AI Hacking key to survival. Logs showed Rael had ordered safety protocols bypassed. Tali found her father's body and a recorded message ordering her to destroy the main geth hub and deliver the data to Xen and Gerrel. The final console proved Rael had deliberately reactivated and networked geth toward sapience for weapons tests, while clearing Tali of any knowledge. Tali begged Shepard not to reveal it, to preserve her father's name.

Back on the Rayya, Shepard could clear Tali via persuasion (30 morality, loyalty gained), lie that no evidence was found (Tali exiled but loyal), rally the crowd with Veetor and Kal'Reegar, or present the evidence (Tali cleared, Rael posthumously exiled, the Fleet Balkanized, loyalty lost). Tali kept the name "vas Normandy" regardless. Rewards included the Energy Drain power for Tali and tech upgrades. The outcome influenced whether quarian-geth peace was possible in Mass Effect 3.

Haestrom was the third planet of the Dholen System, in the Far Rim, and formerly a quarian colony. The quarians established the settlement before the geth revolt roughly 300 years earlier to study the instability of Dholen, the system's parent star, which appeared likely to erupt prematurely into a red giant. As a scientific outpost of minimal military value, Haestrom was poorly equipped to resist geth forces during the insurrection and fell quickly. The planet was lost to the geth in 1896 CE, after which all communication from its surface and attendant space stations ceased.

For the following three centuries the geth established several space stations near Dholen but showed no sign of treating the star as a threat. Dholen's magnetic eruptions and solar output overwhelm most communications in the region, and it was unclear how the geth compensated. Spy probe scans indicated extensive orbital construction around Haestrom housing thousands of geth platforms and an unknown number of geth software "minds." The number of geth on the surface was unknown because Dholen's interference hampered remote scanning. Resource estimates based on geth mining, refining and fabricating practices suggested the planet had at least 20 more years of use before exhaustion; intelligence analysts speculated the geth kept some resources in reserve for repairs.

Captured geth planetary survey data indicated that despite war damage, Haestrom's architecture remained as it had been before the conflict, preserving a quarian architectural style that no longer existed anywhere else in the galaxy. Because Dholen had overwhelmed the planet's protective magnetosphere, humans venturing onto geth-controlled Haestrom faced severe danger: minutes of radiation exposure would overload shields and hours would kill, and solar output rendered surface-to-orbit communication nearly impossible. A travel advisory designated Haestrom a geth stronghold, noting that only military spy drones using cutting-edge stealth technology had returned unharmed from geth space, and prohibited all civilian traffic. Haestrom could not be mined. The planet was the setting for the mission Dossier: Tali in Mass Effect 2, where a quarian research team led by Tali'Zorah investigated Dholen's accelerated aging under geth assault.

*For her gameplay attributes in Mass Effect 2, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 2\)\#Tali'Zorah vas Neema.* “I assumed that you were under cover Shepard \-\- maybe even planning to blow Cerberus up. If that’s the case, I’ll loan you a grenade. Otherwise, I’m here for you, not for them.” After the attack on the SSV Normandy, and having completed her Pilgrimage, Tali joins the crew of the Neema and becomes a respected figure in the Migrant Fleet, earning the title **Tali'Zorah vas Neema**. She also gains a new environmental suit, reflecting her status as a mature adult quarian. In 2185, she leads a mission to the human colony of Freedom's Progress, searching for a missing quarian named Veetor'Nara who had been helping the colonists as part of his Pilgrimage. Tali and her team arrive to find Freedom's Progress eerily deserted, but with the security mechs activated. Tali guesses Veetor is responsible for turning the mechs on. During the search for Veetor, Tali runs into Commander Shepard—who arrived to investigate the disappearances with Jacob Taylor and Miranda Lawson, and whom she believed was long\-dead during the Normandy's destruction. Tali is initially thrilled to find Shepard alive, but is surprised and disappointed to see the Commander working with Cerberus, due to the organization's anti\-alien reputation, and recent act of sabotage against the Flotilla. Tali convinces herself that Shepard is undercover and, hopefully, working to bring Cerberus down. If Shepard gave Tali the data from the rogue geth two years previously, then Shepard could ask Tali if the geth data helped her complete her pilgrimage; to which Tali said that it did, which convinces her that even though the Commander now works for Cerberus, it's still the same Shepard. After finding Veetor, and evidence that the Collectors are behind the colony's disappearance, Shepard decides whether to let Tali return the traumatized quarian back to the Flotilla or hand him over to Cerberus for further interrogation (Tali's response is determined by this decision). Regardless of Shepard's choice, they part ways as Tali returns to the Flotilla: she has an important mission in geth\-controlled space that she couldn't discuss. This mission is, in fact, on the planet Haestrom to gather data on the planet's prematurely dying sun. As Haestrom is deep in geth territory, Tali travels with a contingent of quarian marines, including Kal'Reegar, for protection. Unfortunately, a geth patrol ship sights the quarians and begins dropping troops; the quarian marines are killed and Tali is trapped inside a building with the data she has gathered. Fortunately she is contacted by Shepard, who came to Haestrom in the hope of recruiting her. After fighting their way through the geth, meeting Kal'Reegar, and destroying a powerful Geth Colossus, Shepard's team manages to rescue Tali, who agrees to join Shepard's cause. She explains that the data she has gathered on Haestrom's sun proves it is dying too quickly, possibly (as is elaborated later) due to dark energy affecting the mass of the star. Despondent over the deaths of her friends during the mission, Tali angrily hopes that the Admiralty Board will put this information to good use, and make it worth such a terrible cost. Aboard the Normandy SR\-2, Jacob welcomes Tali warmly, but she dismisses him, reiterating her skepticism towards Cerberus' intentions. She makes it clear that she is joining the mission for Shepard's sake, not Cerberus'; if Shepard dealt with Cerberus experiments back in 2183, Tali reminds the Commander that Cerberus thought that enslaving Thorian Creepers and rachni was a good idea. In parting, Tali is even more disturbed to hear that the new Normandy has an AI.

This Shadow Broker dossier, unlocked after the Lair of the Shadow Broker mission, profiled Tali'Zorah vas Normandy as a mechanic and engineer showing typical quarian investment in her species' future, and noted that her father Rael'Zorah's work was useful for widening geth-quarian tensions.

An email chain records Tali, still Tali'Zorah nar Rayya during her Pilgrimage, contacting the Shadow Broker after finding a recording implicating Spectre Saren working with the geth and the Reapers, offering the information in exchange for protection. The Broker directed her to his Citadel enforcer Fist, but secretly ordered Fist: "When you get the intel, kill the quarian and any of our operatives who had access to the data." Tali then reported that Fist tried to sell her to Saren and that she had instead given the information to "a human Alliance commander named Shepard."

A keystroke log captures her repeatedly drafting and erasing a condolence letter to the parents of Myrr'Jorin, a soldier killed on Haestrom saving her life, struggling over wording such as "He gave his life to get data that will one day bring us back to Homeworld... and we all honor his sacrifice," before saving the draft and exiting without sending it.

Tali'Zorah nar Rayya was born in 2161 aboard the liveship Rayya to Rael'Zorah of the quarian Admiralty Board. A mechanical genius, she left the Migrant Fleet on her Pilgrimage, the quarian rite of passage into adulthood. In Mass Effect: Homeworlds she traveled aboard the Honorata with Keenah'Breizh, extracted a geth memory core containing a recording of an attack planned on Eden Prime and the coming of the Reapers, and was hunted across Illium and onto the Citadel by the turian mercenary Jacobus, working for Saren Arterius. Keenah died; Tali trapped Jacobus in an incinerator and burned him alive, then sought an information broker to reach the Council.

In Mass Effect, Fist betrayed her to Saren's agents; ambushed near Chora's Den, Tali threw a tech proximity mine and was saved by Commander Shepard. Her data provided proof that got Saren's Spectre status revoked and the first mention of the Reapers and the Conduit. She joined Shepard's crew, working in the Normandy's engine room with Engineer Adams, and shared insight into quarian nomad life and the geth. In an optional assignment she could receive rogue geth data to complete her Pilgrimage; refusing it caused her to leave the crew afterward.

In Mass Effect 2, having completed her Pilgrimage, she joined the Neema and became Tali'Zorah vas Neema. Shepard met her on Freedom's Progress hunting Veetor'Nara, then recruited her on Haestrom, where a geth patrol killed her marine escort; she and Kal'Reegar survived and she brought data proving Haestrom's sun was dying prematurely. She joined Shepard for Shepard's sake, not Cerberus's. Her loyalty mission, Tali: Treason, changed her name to Tali'Zorah vas Normandy. She is a romance option for a male Shepard, culminating before the Omega 4 relay when she removes her mask; if she survives, "it was totally worth it."

In Mass Effect 3, if she survived the Suicide Mission, she returned to the Fleet, becoming an Admiral in her father's place (or a secret adviser if exiled) during the war to retake Rannoch. She served as geth software expert aboard the geth dreadnought and on Rannoch, where she claimed a patch of land and Shepard handed her a rock. At the climax, if Shepard upgraded the geth she watched the Migrant Fleet burn, removed her mask, whispered "I'm sorry," and threw herself off a cliff. If Shepard stopped the upload she stabbed the geth unit with her boot knife; if Legion survived and peace was brokered, she confirmed the geth had souls. Surviving, she rejoined the Normandy and could become the quarian ambassador on the Citadel. If romanced, she left Shepard a photo of her unmasked face, and at the final battle, gravely wounded, told Shepard "I have a home" and begged him to return.

evidence.section: Bio\-Trivia: Tali's Name Used to Be Talsi
evidence.text: Coming up with the names for alien species is one thing. Finding names for individual alien characters is a heck of a hard thing to brainstorm. Writers will end up with pages of weird words before settling on one that sounds weird in just the right way. Sometimes, a word will be close, and all that's needed is to take out a letter, as in the case of iconic quarian squad mate Tali, who was originally Talsi.

The Alliance Military Vocational Code system classifies the career path of all serving personnel. The MVC consists of one letter and one number. A soldier's MVC indicates proficiency, not rank. The letter notes career path; the number indicates level of experience, as indicated by service record, technical scores, and commendations. All 26 letters are used, and numbers run from 1 to 7\. N is the letter code for Special Forces personnel.

Anjik's relatives include her mother, Lavaala, Falet, and Arjaan Do Xeel. Arjaan died defending Techiix, taking nearly a dozen kett with him, and was deemed a hero by his immediate superior officer. Anjik tried to break the news of his death to her mother, but the message remained an unsent draft in one of the computers in the base. The Resistance commander has a cordial relationship with fellow Resistance fighter Jaal Ama Darav, self\-appointed observer to the newly\-arrived aliens from another galaxy.

The Broker Terminal was a message terminal in Liara T'Soni's cabin aboard the Normandy SR-2 in Mass Effect 3. It held correspondence and intercepted communications collected through Liara's work as the Shadow Broker, covering events across the galaxy during the Reaper War. The page reproduces its contents in full.

Many entries concerned the Crucible project: Kahlee Sanders wrote to David Anderson about the breathtaking device she was helping build; Dr. Lok reported to Admiral Hackett on nervous staff reactions to rachni working on the Crucible; Mordin Solus messaged an STG colleague about the Crucible's scale and Alliance engineers slavishly following the Mars Archive plans; Dr. Cole and Dr. T'Kisha described engineering and material shortages solved by anonymous Shadow Broker deliveries of platinum and a comm server retrieved by Kasumi Goto. Kahlee Sanders also called Jack about securing an L3-X1 biotic amp for the Grissom Academy students.

Other logs included Grunt addressing new Aralahk Company recruits, Sergeant Cavanagh apologizing for firing on allied geth primes, a purchase list for Zaeed Massani, Jacob Taylor's love letter to Dr. Brynn Cole, three unsent letters from Morinth (signed Mirala) to her sisters Rila and Falere reporting Samara's death, and Alliance correspondence to Miranda Lawson thanking her for intelligence on Cerberus. Councilor Gujir was recorded authorizing seizure of Senate eezo stockpiles to evacuate a colony. A smuggler manifest in the Yungiss system led to batarian slaves being granted asylum at the Broker's request. Feron reported to the Broker on scouting the Terminus Systems with Tazzik. An extensive set of Liara's "Prothean Notes" (2171-2186) traced her academic career, her realization that the Collectors were husked Protheans, and her shifting, disillusioned view of the Protheans after meeting Javik, ending with a list of possible book titles for a work she hoped to co-write with him.
**Prerequisite:** Citadel: Leviathan III (Mass Effect 3\) It is named after "Psi", the Greek letter, and "Tophet", a sacrificial pyre in Jerusalem.

evidence.section: Emails from Morinth \[Never read by recipients]
evidence.text: Letter 1: Rila and Falere, I know we haven't spoken since I left. I understand that after what mother probably told you about me, you'll be suspicious. But you have the right to learn that Samara died fighting the Collectors in the Omega 4 relay. I was on Omega when I heard the news. Mother was a little closer to you two, and you deserve to know she passed on while chasing the justice she loved so much. I'm sure her last thoughts must have been of you. Take care of yourselves, Your sister Letter 2: Dear Rila and Falere, I wish I could show you some of the amazing places I've been. I've seen the galaxy's tallest skyscrapers on Illium, floated around zero\-gravity gardens on a quarian ship, even returned to Armali on Thessia. Do you still remember it, from when we were young? I ache when I think you two are closed off from everything. I respect your choice to stay in that cold Monastery, but not that they cloister you like children. Your sister Letter 3: Dear Sisters: This must be my last letter, but I miss you. I need to let you know how much I wish we could meet again, even be together again. Your monastery isn't impossible to leave, if you truly wanted to see the galaxy. I don't think that freedom would be so wrong. And it could be someday soon. Yours, Mirala

This Shadow Broker dossier, unlocked after the Lair of the Shadow Broker mission, profiled Jacob Taylor as an ex-Alliance soldier with biotic training and a solid service record, whom the Broker judged had been placed on Shepard's team mainly as a stabilizing personality.

It compiled his most recent workout stats (hundreds of crunches, squat thrusts, leg lifts and half sit-ups) and his preferred workout viewing, including Blasto: The Jellyfish Stings and its making-of, Old Yeller: Centennial Remastered Edition, and Asari Confessions 26: True Blue.

A military letter dated February 19, 2184, from Col. Hashim Banks of the First Earth Division Special Forces, expressed regret at Taylor's resignation from the Alliance military, praised him as an exemplary marine, and offered him a promotion to First Lieutenant with a pay raise if he would join Banks's company.

A personal letter from his father, Ronald Taylor, written as a just-in-case message before the Gernsback traveled too far from its last relay, admitted that he had not been around enough for his son, said the expedition's money was meant to buy a quiet life far from space with Jacob and his mother, and told Jacob he was proud of the man he had become. The letter closes: "I love you, son, and I'm proud of the man you've become. I wish I could have told you that one last time." The Gernsback was the ship whose survivors Taylor later encounters.

This page collects Tali'Zorah's squad-specific lines across all three games: unique dialogue at scripted story points, "talk to squadmate" location comments, spontaneous combat and banter lines, and secret dialogue only reachable by editing her into the party. The material recurringly touches quarian themes (the Migrant Fleet, homelessness, the geth, her mistrust of the Council and Cerberus), her fear of spiders, her drone Chatika vas Paus, and her running commentary comparing alien worlds to the flotilla. Representative lines:

- Tali, on Noveria when Captain Matsuo says Shepard is far from home: "Home is a state of mind."
- Tali, first seeing the Thorian on Feros: "Keelah, what is that?"
- Tali, at the salarian camp on Virmire before the assault: "These salarians are willing to die to stop Saren... and so am I." / (if Wrex lives) "I will fight with fire for you, Commander."
- Tali, on Ilos: "We shouldn't be here. Not us. Not the geth. Not Saren."
- Tali, if chosen to lead the second diversion squad and killed during the Suicide Mission: "There were too many. Lost my shields. Suit ruptures... too many... Keelah se'lai..."
- Tali, summoning her combat drone: "Go for the optics, Chatika! Go for the optics!" / "Nothing's faster than Chatika vas Paus!"
- Tali, using AI Hacking on geth: "We made you, we can break you!"
- Tali, in the Silver Coast Casino when a female Shepard comments on her enviro-suit: "At least you can dress up. What can I do? I'm already wearing my two sexiest belts!"
- Tali, to the Shepard clone in the Citadel Archives after it threatens to open her helmet: "just a cheap imitation of the real thing."
- Tali, spontaneously on the Attican Traverse krogan mission when Swarmers appear: "spiders, spiders, spiders, spiders!"
- Tali, cursing Kai Leng on Thessia: "Bosh'tet!"
- Tali, disembarking the Normandy after the Citadel ambush: "Worst shore leave ever."

Tali's Trial Aboard the Rayya. 2185, some time after Tali rejoined Shepard the liveship Rayya at the Migrant Fleet — the garden plaza, then the hearing chamber Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib-Qwib, the Board's outspoken geth sympathiser, objects to Shepard defending Tali at all — "a human has no business in such sensitive military matters" — and Shala'Raan overrules him, since Koris himself declared Tali crew of the Normandy SR-2. If Legion is present he objects instead that the geth should be removed from the courtroom, accusing Tali of trying to intimidate the admirals, and withdraws when reminded the Rayya's captain permitted Legion aboard. Later, quick to assume Shepard and Tali died retaking the Alarei, he moves to have Tali posthumously exiled, drawing sharp objections from Raan and Gerrel. Afterward Shepard can privately endorse or condemn his ideals.

Recruiting Tali on Haestrom. 2185, after Horizon, deep in geth-controlled space the ruined quarian research site on Haestrom, under its dying sun If Legion is in the squad, Tali opens fire on it, shouting a warning about enemy geth; Legion takes cover, and Tali agrees to defer the argument.
